Amy — thanks for the clear asks. Summary below and proposed actions so we’re all aligned before legal redlines: 

1) Activation fee: Redwood can issue a standalone invoice for the activation charge dated on commencement. That invoice will be separate from usage billing.

2) Usage billing cadence: We propose monthly usage invoices in arrears (itemized by route/model). The current draft had a quarterly band for committed tranches; we will remove that and make the order form show monthly invoicing for usage.

3) Net terms: Our standard is Net30. For this deal we can approve Net45 for the customer finance entity on the condition the invoiced entity remains the US operating entity (no multi-entity split). Kimberly, can we confirm finance/legal comfort with Net45 on a US remit?

4) VAT / Gross-up: If Lumen’s EU subsidiaries require a VAT reverse charge, we’ll accept evidence-based VAT handling. We’d ask for the completed tax certificate before the first EU invoice.

Next steps (action items):
- Jonas: update Order Form (pricing table + invoice cadence) and re-issue v3 by EOD. (I’ll attach version notes)
- Kimberly: advise on Net45 approval scope and prepare a short clause we can insert stating "Net45 accepted by Redwood for the US invoiced entity only; multi-entity invoicing requires further sign-off."
- Karthik: follow up with Amy on timing for CFO approval if Net45 requires it.

All —

I reviewed Jonas’ summary. From a legal/finance perspective we can accept Net45 for the US billed entity only with these safeguards: 

- Clause language: "Redwood agrees to Net45 payment terms for invoices issued to the Customer's designated US entity only. If invoices are to be issued to any non-US entity, standard Net30 applies unless otherwise agreed in writing by Redwood's finance team."

- Accounting control: We require the PO or procurement confirmation to name the invoiced legal entity exactly as on the W-9 / tax certificate. If the procurement PO later requests entity swap, Redwood reserves the right to re-invoice and adjust billing dates (no retroactive Net45 acceptance).

- VAT handling: For EU subsidiaries, Redwood will rely on a completed VAT evidence form prior to first EU invoice. If evidence is not provided, Redwood will invoice gross (including VAT) and reserve the right to issue a credit/adjustment after evidence is supplied.

I’ve drafted the clause text below for insertion; happy to add it to the Order Form language in the redline:

"Net Payment Terms and Invoice Entity: Redwood Inference will honor net payment terms of forty-five (45) days for invoices issued to the Customer's United States entity expressly identified in the Order Form. Customer must provide tax and entity evidence as requested prior to issuance of invoices to non-US entities."

Karthik — I’ll approve the Net45 for this deal now. Jonas — please include the exact invoiced entity name and attach the tax certificate to the Order Form before sending to signature.
